# Fixtures

`fake-claude.mjs` records test-only argv/stdin/cwd/selected env, emits deterministic version/output/exit behavior, and can create a process-group descendant. Its lifecycle mode records both leader and descendant PIDs and emits readiness only after cleanup handlers are installed. It is never copied into a release.

`mcp_oauth_fixture_manifest.mjs` pins the official MCP Python SDK `v2.0.0` commit and simple-auth example path used by the executable Runtime qualification. `mcp_oauth_capture_server.py` delegates all DCR, PKCE, authorization, token, and MCP authentication behavior to that official provider, adds only an explicitly configured bounded delay, optional official `TokenError(invalid_grant)`, and a serialized-response hook that removes `token_type` from successful responses beginning with the second exchange. It records redirect URIs, hashed client identities, fixed mutation events, lifecycle events, and boolean authenticated checks—never token values or user configuration—and neither fixture is copied into a release.

`pty_cli_driver.py` mirrors Dream's `pty.openpty` boundary with ECHO disabled and attaches candidate stdin/stdout/stderr to the same slave. It only proxies master bytes and input, owns no protocol state, terminates its process group on cleanup, and is never packaged.
